## Overview

This document specifies the **internal API** that decouples
exploreDE's server modules from the on-disk format of the data they
visualise. Today, modules read directly from a SUSHI / proteomics
`SummarizedExperiment` via a deconstructed `gStoreList`. After this
work, modules call accessors on a single R6 instance — `eds` —
backed by whichever concrete subclass matches the input. Today that
is a per-shape `ExploreDatasetSE_*` wrapper around the legacy SE;
when upstream producers emit canonical `.h5ad` directly, a single
`ExploreDatasetH5AD` peer subclass reads from an in-memory
`anndataR::AnnData` conforming to the
[2026-04-17 AnnData spec](anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd). Modules don't
notice the difference.

### Goals

1. **Storage-format agnostic.** Server modules see one accessor API
   regardless of what produced the data. Adding a new on-disk format
   later is one new subclass, not a sprawl through every server
   module.
2. **FGCZ-agnostic. exploreDE works on anyone's data, anywhere.**
   The current app hard-couples to gStore/pStore paths, LDAP auth,
   SUSHI `param$*` conventions, and FGCZ-specific factor encoding
   (`[Factor]` colData suffix, `^constrast_` rowData nesting). The
   target is a tool researchers anywhere can point at their own
   data — counts CSV + sample sheet, or a `.h5ad` they built
   themselves — and have the app load and visualise it without
   needing FGCZ infrastructure. The canonical AnnData layout is the
   contract that makes this possible; see the AnnData spec's
   [§"Minimum viable AnnData"](anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd) for the
   smallest valid input. BYOD UX work (vignettes, CSV→h5ad helper,
   friendly validator errors) is Phase 4a (§7.6).
3. **No feature loss.** Every existing tab, plot, filter, and
   download keeps working. The migration is non-disruptive — Phase 1
   ships a legacy compatibility shim so server modules can be
   migrated one at a time without ever leaving master broken.
4. **Multi-omics ready.** Genomics (RNA-seq, CRISPR), proteomics
   (protein, peptide, phospho), and future metabolomics / lipidomics
   all flow through the same code path.

### Three fronts of the larger migration

This spec is the consumer-side piece. The full migration spans three
fronts (see directory `README.md`):

1. **Upstream producers** emit canonical `.h5ad` directly — separate
   workstream, tracked in
   [`producer_migration_2026-04-30.md`](producer_migration_2026-04-30.md).
   Until producers migrate, exploreDE reads the legacy SEs through
   per-shape SE subclasses.
2. **Canonical on-disk format** — defined in
   [`anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd`](anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd).
3. **Downstream consumer** — exploreDE reads through the class
   hierarchy. **This spec.**

### Validation

The design was validated against six real datasets via
[`poc_explore_dataset_2026-04-30.R`](poc_explore_dataset_2026-04-30.R).
A canonical-converter alternative (single `ExploreDatasetH5AD` reader
plus an SE → AnnData normaliser at load time) was considered and
rejected; see Appendix A for the summary.

### Reading order

If you're new: read this overview, then §1 (architecture) and §2
(accessor contract). Skip ahead to §7 (phasing) when you're ready to
plan implementation work; consult §6 (migration map) per-module
during Phase 2.

---

## 1. Architecture

A small R6 class hierarchy. The abstract `ExploreDataset` base
defines the accessor contract; an abstract `ExploreDatasetSE`
intermediate holds the shared SE plumbing; concrete subclasses
handle each SE shape. A future `ExploreDatasetH5AD` subclass is the
peer of `ExploreDatasetSE` — same parent, same accessor signatures,
different backend.

### 1.1 Class hierarchy

```
ExploreDataset                (abstract base — config-only accessors)
├── ExploreDatasetSE          (abstract intermediate — SE backend ref, shared plumbing)
│   ├── ExploreDatasetSE_RNASeq        (DESeq2 / EdgeR / Limma, top-level rowData + DE inline)
│   ├── ExploreDatasetSE_CountQC       (top-level rowData, no DE)
│   │   └── ExploreDatasetSE_CrisprCountQC  (+ sgrna_to_gene)
│   └── ExploreDatasetSE_Proteomics    (nested rowData$constrast_*, built feature_id)
└── ExploreDatasetH5AD        (peer of ExploreDatasetSE; lands Phase 3)
```

Naming: `ExploreDatasetSE_<shape>`, `ExploreDatasetH5AD`.

### 1.2 The intermediate: `ExploreDatasetSE`

Holds `private$.se` (the legacy SE) and implements every read method
in terms of two private hooks the subclass overrides:

- `.build_config(se)` — returns the per-instance config list at
  `$initialize()` time
- `.prep()` — populates `private$.features_df`,
  `private$.de_dfs`, `private$.fid_lookup` from the SE

Everything else is uniform across SE shapes: `samples()`,
`features()`, `de(c)`, `assay(name)`, `enrichment(c, kind)`,
`enrichment_input(c)` all read from the prepared internal slots.

### 1.3 The concrete SE subclasses

Each implements `.build_config()` + `.prep()` only. The shape-specific
quirks live here and nowhere else:

| Subclass | data_type | DE source | feature_id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_RNASeq` | `rna_seq` | inline in `rowData(se)` (single contrast from `param$comparison`) | identity (`rownames(se)`) |
| `_CountQC` | `count_qc` | none | identity |
| `_CrisprCountQC` | `crispr_count_qc` | none (inherits `_CountQC$.prep()`) | identity; adds `sgrna_to_gene` map parsed from `rownames(se)` |
| `_Proteomics` | `proteomics` | nested `rowData(se)$constrast_<name>` DataFrames | **built** via `protein_Id [+site/+peptide_Id]`; `.fid_lookup` remaps assay rownames |

The reference implementation is
[`poc_explore_dataset_2026-04-30.R`](poc_explore_dataset_2026-04-30.R)
— every non-trivial method body in this spec mirrors what's in the
POC.

### 1.4 The factory: `new_explore_dataset()`

```r
new_explore_dataset(input):
  se <- (load SE from path / URL / direct SE object)
  shape <- detect_se_shape(se)        # rna_seq | count_qc | crispr_count_qc | proteomics
  cls <- switch(shape,
    rna_seq         = ExploreDatasetSE_RNASeq,
    count_qc        = ExploreDatasetSE_CountQC,
    crispr_count_qc = ExploreDatasetSE_CrisprCountQC,
    proteomics      = ExploreDatasetSE_Proteomics
  )
  cls$new(se)
```

`detect_se_shape()` reads `metadata(se)$param$comparison`,
`rowData(se)` column names, and `rownames(se)` patterns to classify.
The factory is the **only place** SE-shape detection lives; subclasses
trust they were instantiated correctly.

Once `ExploreDatasetH5AD` lands (Phase 3), the factory grows one
branch — if the input is a `.h5ad` file (or a live `AnnData`), it
bypasses SE-shape detection entirely and returns
`ExploreDatasetH5AD$new(adata)`.

### 1.5 The future peer: `ExploreDatasetH5AD`

A single concrete subclass reading from a live
`anndataR::AnnData` that conforms to the canonical layout (the
[2026-04-17 AnnData spec](anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd)).

| Method               | Reads from                          |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `samples()`          | `adata$obs` (strip `factor_` prefix) |
| `features()`         | `adata$var` + computed `display_name` from `label_*` fallback chain |
| `assay(name, ...)`   | `t(adata$X)` if name is the omics-X-name, else `t(adata$layers[[name]])` |
| `contrasts()`        | `sub("^de_", "", grep("^de_", names(adata$varm)))` |
| `de(c)`              | `as.data.frame(adata$varm[[paste0("de_", c)]])` |
| `contrast_meta(c)`   | `adata$uns$de[[c]]` |
| `enrichment(c, kind)`| `adata$uns$enrichment_native[[c]]` filtered by kind |
| `data_type()`        | `adata$uns$omics_type` |
| `factor_names()`     | `sub("^factor_", "", grep("^factor_", colnames(obs)))` |

No `data_type` branching in any read method — the canonical AnnData
layout is uniform across omics. The reader walks slots.

**One H5AD subclass for every omics.** Genomics, proteomics,
metabolomics, lipidomics all read through this same class once their
producers emit canonical `.h5ad`. The omics-type axis is carried by
`uns["omics_type"]`, `uns["hierarchy"]`, and `var["label_*"]` columns
— not by class polymorphism.

### 1.6 Adding a new backend later

A future Parquet / Zarr / DuckDB backend: write one peer subclass
(`ExploreDatasetParquet`, etc.) inheriting from `ExploreDataset`,
implementing the same accessor signatures. Add one branch in the
factory. The SE subclasses and H5AD subclass are unaffected.

### 1.7 SE → `.h5ad` export

Not derived automatically from the SE subclass design (unlike the
canonical-converter alternative — see Appendix A). The export path
is documented in `build_example_anndata.R` as a standalone reference
script: `convert_rnaseq()` / `convert_crispr_countqc()` /
`convert_proteomics()` produce canonical AnnData from each legacy SE
shape; `anndataR::write_h5ad()` serialises to disk. This is the
reference for upstream producers (front 1); the same logic can land
inside the package as `$as_anndata()` methods on each SE subclass if
we want per-instance export from a running app.

## 2. Accessor contract

The public API exploreDE modules call. Same names, same return types
across all backends.

| Method                                   | Returns                                                                  |
|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `eds$omics_class()`                      | `character(1)` — umbrella discipline: `"genomics"` \| `"proteomics"` \| (future: `"metabolomics"`) |
| `eds$data_type()`                        | `character(1)` — flavour within omics_class: `"RNASeq"` \| `"CountQC"` \| `"CrisprCountQC"` \| `"proteomics"` \| `"peptidomics"` \| `"phosphoproteomics"` |
| `eds$has_de()` / `$has_enrichment()`     | `logical(1)`                                                            |
| `eds$organism()` / `$ref_build()`        | `character(1)` or `NA`                                                  |
| `eds$feature_id_kind()`                  | `character(1)` (`gene`/`isoform`/`protein`/`peptide`/`site`/…)         |
| `eds$samples()`                          | `data.frame`, rownames = sample ids, factor cols typed                  |
| `eds$sample_ids()` / `$n_samples()`      | `character`, `integer(1)`                                               |
| `eds$sample_factor(factor)`              | `character`/`factor` — single column from `samples()`; convenience shorthand |
| `eds$factor_names()`                     | `character`                                                             |
| `eds$factor_levels(f)`                   | `character`, canonical order                                            |
| `eds$primary_grouping()`                 | `character(1)`                                                          |
| `eds$features()`                         | `data.frame`, rownames = feature_id, includes computed `display_name`   |
| `eds$feature_ids()` / `$n_features()`    | `character`, `integer(1)`                                               |
| `eds$feature_display(ids)`               | `character`, named by feature_id                                        |
| `eds$assay_names()` / `$has_assay(n)`    | `character`, `logical(1)`                                               |
| `eds$assay(name, features=, samples=)`   | `numeric matrix`, features × samples                                    |
| `eds$assay_label(name)`                  | `character(1)` — human-readable UI label for a canonical assay name (e.g. `"normalised_log2"` → `"Normalised + Log2"`); falls back to `name` if no label registered |
| `eds$raw_assay()` / `$primary_assay()`   | `numeric matrix`                                                        |
| `eds$contrasts()` / `$primary_contrast()`| `character`, `character(1)`                                             |
| `eds$de(contrast)`                       | `data.frame` with canonical cols `effect_log2fc`, `score_pvalue`, `score_fdr` (per AnnData spec) |
| `eds$de_all()`                           | named `list` of data.frames                                             |
| `eds$contrast_meta(c)`                   | `list` with `test_group`, `reference_group`, `factor_name`, `method`    |
| `eds$contrast_label(c)`                  | `character(1)` — validates contrast exists and returns the canonical key (already in `test_vs_reference` form). Modules wanting prose can `gsub("_vs_", " vs ", x)`. |
| `eds$enrichment_kinds()`                 | `character` ⊆ `c("ora","gsea")`                                         |
| `eds$enrichment(c, kind)`                | named `list` of `clusterProfiler::enrichResult` (ora) or `gseaResult` (gsea); empty list if not run |
| `eds$enrichment_input(c)`                | `list(seq_anno, ranked_l2fc, selections)` (derived on the fly under the canonical schema) |
| `eds$go_terms(ids=, ontology=)`          | `data.frame` long format (feature_id, ontology, go_id, term_name) — **not yet implemented**; no current consumer after `server-goTile.R` migrated to `all_pathways()`. |
| `eds$all_pathways()`                     | `character` vector of `"GO:XXXXXXX term name"` strings for selectize dropdowns. Implemented on base class via `self$features()` GO columns + `clusterProfiler::go2term()`. Returns `character(0)` when GO columns absent. |
| `eds$sgrna_to_gene()`                    | named `character` or `NULL`                                             |
| `eds$proteomics_choices(kind)`           | `list(choices, lookup)` or `NULL`                                       |
| `eds$source()`                           | `list` (provenance)                                                     |
| `eds$backend()`                          | the underlying SE (today) or AnnData (Phase 3+). **Escape hatch — see §5.2.** |
| `eds$backend_kind()`                     | `"se"` or `"h5ad"` — for the rare caller that must dispatch              |

**Invariant**: `eds$enrichment(c, kind)` always returns a list of
`clusterProfiler` objects (or empty list); never `NULL`, never raw
data.frames. Modules can pass results straight to
`enrichplot::dotplot()` / `gseaplot2()` etc.

## 3. Configuration

Each instance carries a per-instance `private$.config` list, built
once in `.build_config(se)` and read by the config-only accessors
(`data_type`, `factors`, `assay_map`, `contrast_meta`, etc.). The
schema is documented in the POC's `.build_config()` bodies; spec
fields are exhaustively listed in `module_inventory_2026-04-30.md`
§3 (validated against codebase usage).

For the H5AD subclass, the equivalent information is read directly
from `adata$uns` / `adata$obs` / `adata$var` — no separate config
list is needed because the canonical AnnData is self-describing. The
H5AD subclass's accessor bodies do the lookup inline (per §1.5
table).

The mapping between SUSHI's `metadata(se)$param` fields and the
canonical AnnData slots is documented in
[`anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd` §"SUSHI decoupling — what goes away"](anndata_spec_2026-04-17.qmd).

## 4. Validation

Two validators ship in Phase 0 (§7.2). Both important.

### 4.1 Object validator

`validate_explore_dataset(eds, strict = TRUE)` — runtime invariants
on the live `eds` instance. Subclass-agnostic — runs through
accessors:

1. **Concrete subclass**: `inherits(eds, "ExploreDataset")` and the
   runtime class is one of the concrete subclasses (an SE subclass
   today, the H5AD subclass once it lands) — not the abstract base
   or intermediate.
2. **Cross-references resolve**:
   - Every `eds$factor_names()[i]` is a column in `eds$samples()`.
   - Every `eds$contrasts()[c]` resolves: calling `eds$de(c)`
     succeeds.
   - `eds$primary_grouping() ∈ eds$factor_names()`.
   - `eds$primary_contrast() ∈ eds$contrasts() ∪ NA`.
3. **Sample / feature alignment**: `colnames(eds$raw_assay())` ==
   `eds$sample_ids()`; `rownames(eds$raw_assay())` ==
   `eds$feature_ids()`.

Cost is proportional to the number of contrasts (one `eds$de(c)`
round-trip each) plus one each of `samples()`, `features()`,
`assay_names()`, `raw_assay()`.

### 4.2 Schema validator (h5ad only)

`validate_anndata_schema(adata, strict = TRUE)` — invariants on a
`.h5ad` file or in-memory `AnnData` per the AnnData spec
§"Validator". Only runs when the input is an h5ad / AnnData (i.e.
when `ExploreDatasetH5AD$new()` is being called, or when validating
a producer-side output). The SE subclasses don't go through this
validator because they don't produce canonical AnnData at load time.

1. `uns$schema_version == "exploreDE/1.0"`.
2. `uns$omics_type` in the allowlist.
3. `obs_names` and `var_names` unique strings.
4. For each `varm[de_*]`: required cols `effect_log2fc`,
   `score_pvalue`, `score_fdr`; row count == `n_vars`; key exists in
   `uns$de`.
5. For each `uns$de[<c>]`: required fields `assay_used`,
   `factor_used`, `test_group`, `reference_group`; cross-refs
   resolve.
6. Hierarchy declaration matches `hierarchy_*` columns in `var`.
7. `factor_*` colData columns are categorical with explicit levels.

The schema validator may land in Phase 3 (when the H5AD subclass
arrives) rather than Phase 0 — it has no SE-side consumer.

## 5. Cross-cutting concerns

### 5.1 Caching strategy: there isn't one (in the class)

Methods are pure backend reads. Every `eds$samples()`,
`eds$assay("counts")`, `eds$de(c)` reaches through to the SE (or
AnnData).

The cache is the **Shiny reactive graph**. Server modules wrap any
expensive accessor in a `reactive()`, and Shiny memoises at exactly
the right granularity:

```r
# Correct usage:
de_table <- reactive({
  eds <- inputDataReactive()$.eds
  eds$de(input$contrast)        # only re-runs when input$contrast changes
})

# Within one reactive evaluation, extract once if reused:
plot_data <- reactive({
  eds <- inputDataReactive()$.eds
  cd  <- eds$samples()
  cts <- eds$assay("counts")
  build_plot(cd, cts, …)
})
```

Reasons:

- **Shiny is already a memoisation engine.** A second cache inside
  the class would double-cache and add a second invalidation story.
- **Class becomes simpler.** No `.cache` field, no `.cached()`
  helper, no `invalidate_cache()` method.
- **Cheap reads stay cheap.** `colData` / `rowData` are already in
  memory.

For non-Shiny callers (tests, scripts), extract to a local if you'll
reuse:

```r
de <- eds$de("treated_vs_control")
plot_volcano(de); plot_ma(de); save_csv(de)
```

If a non-Shiny use case ever needs aggressive memoisation, write a
thin `with_cache(eds)` decorator class then. We do not ship one in
Phase 0 — YAGNI.

### 5.2 Backend escape hatch

`eds$backend()` returns the underlying object (a
`SummarizedExperiment` for the SE subclasses today; an
`anndataR::AnnData` for the H5AD subclass when it lands).
`eds$backend_kind()` returns `"se"` or `"h5ad"` for callers that
must dispatch. Used by:

- Methods-text generation (provenance).
- Download handlers (legacy `.rds` download, or
  `anndataR::write_h5ad(eds$backend(), path)` once `backend_kind() == "h5ad"`).
- Debugging.

**Forbidden** in module read paths. If a module thinks it needs
`eds$backend()` to access data, it needs a new accessor instead.
Code-review rule, not a runtime check.

## 6. Migration map: today's reads → new accessor calls

Every read pattern that exists in `inst/app/server-*.R` today, paired
with its replacement. Drives Phase 2 PRs (§7.4).

### 6.1 Direct SE accesses (must die)

| Today                                            | Replacement                                  |
|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `assay(inputDataReactive()$se, "counts")`        | `eds$assay("counts")`                        |
| `assay(se, "presentFlag")`                       | `eds$assay("present_flag")`                  |
| `assays(se)`, `names(assays(se))`                | `eds$assay_names()`                          |
| `rowData(se)$gene_name`                          | `eds$features()$label_gene_symbol`           |
| `rowData(se)[[paste0("constrast_", c)]]`         | `eds$de(c)`                                  |
| `colData(se)`                                    | `eds$samples()`                              |
| `rownames(se)` / `nrow(se)` / `ncol(se)`         | `eds$feature_ids()` / `eds$n_*()`            |
| `metadata(se)$param$<x>`                         | see §6.2                                     |
| `metadata(se)$enrichResult`                      | `eds$enrichment(c, "ora")`                   |
| `metadata(se)$enrichResultGSEA`                  | `eds$enrichment(c, "gsea")`                  |
| `metadata(se)$enrichInput`                       | `eds$enrichment_input(c)`                    |
| `inputDataReactive()$seUnfiltered`               | `eds$assay("counts_unfiltered")`             |

### 6.2 SUSHI param fields → API methods

| `metadata(se)$param$X`   | Replacement                                            |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `sampleGroup`            | `eds$contrast_meta(c)$test_group`                      |
| `refGroup`               | `eds$contrast_meta(c)$reference_group`                 |
| `groupingName`           | `eds$primary_grouping()`                               |
| `featureLevel`           | `eds$feature_id_kind()`                                |
| `comparison`             | `eds$contrasts()` / `eds$primary_contrast()`           |
| `backgroundExpression`   | absorbed into `assay("normalised_log2")` computation   |
| `refBuild`               | `eds$ref_build()`                                      |
| `runGO`                  | `eds$has_enrichment()`                                 |
| `fdrThreshORA`, `fdrThreshGSEA`, `pValThreshGO`, `log2RatioThreshGO` | `eds$contrast_meta(c)$thresholds[[...]]` (where present) |

### 6.3 `gStoreList` fields → API methods

| `inputDataReactive()$X`  | Replacement                                            |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `dataType`               | `eds$data_type()` for exact flavour; `eds$omics_class()` for umbrella dispatch (`"genomics"` \| `"proteomics"`) — use omics_class when branching between all genomics vs all proteomics types |
| `seqAnno`                | `eds$de(eds$primary_contrast())`                       |
| `seqAnnoList`            | `eds$de_all()`                                         |
| `countList` (dropdown UI)| `setNames(eds$assay_names(), vapply(eds$assay_names(), eds$assay_label, character(1)))` — canonical names as values, human-readable labels as display names |
| `countList[[input$x]]`   | `eds$assay(input$x)` — input now stores the canonical assay name |
| `countList[["Raw"]]`     | `eds$assay("counts")`                                  |
| `countList[["Normalised"]]`        | `eds$assay("normalised")`                    |
| `countList[["Normalised + Log2"]]` | `eds$assay("normalised_log2")`               |
| `countList[["VST"]]`     | `eds$assay("vst")`                                     |
| `countList[["FPKM"]]`    | `eds$assay("fpkm")`                                    |
| `countList[["TPM"]]`     | `eds$assay("tpm")`                                     |
| `dataset`                | `eds$samples()`                                        |
| `factors`                | `eds$factor_names()`                                   |
| `factorLevels`           | `eds$factor_levels(f)` per `f`                         |
| `factorNames`            | `eds$factor_names()`                                   |
| `groupingName`           | `eds$primary_grouping()`                               |
| `genes`                  | `eds$feature_ids()`                                    |
| `gene_choices`, `gene_lookup`, `protein_choices`, `protein_lookup` | `eds$proteomics_choices("gene"\|"protein")` |
| `sgRNA_to_gene`          | `eds$sgrna_to_gene()`                                  |
| `goObjects`              | `eds$enrichment(c, "ora"\|"gsea")`                     |
| `goObjects$runGO`        | `eds$has_enrichment()`                                 |
| `allPathways`            | `eds$all_pathways()`                                   |
| `contrasts`              | `eds$contrasts()`                                      |
| `design`, `designLevels` | `eds$contrast_meta(c)$test_group` / `$reference_group` |
| `param`                  | DELETED — fields go through §6.2                       |
| `se`, `seUnfiltered`     | `eds$backend()` (escape hatch only — see §5.2)         |

### 6.4 DE column rename at the boundary

The API exposes AnnData-canonical names (`effect_log2fc` /
`score_pvalue` / `score_fdr`). Modules currently using `log2Ratio` /
`pValue` / `fdr` rename at the existing `dplyr::select()` boundary —
typically one line per module:

```r
seqAnnoFilt <- eds$de(input$contrastSelected) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    feature_id,
    log2Ratio = effect_log2fc,
    pValue    = score_pvalue,
    fdr       = score_fdr
  )
# Rest of the module continues to use log2Ratio / pValue / fdr unchanged.
```

## 7. Implementation phasing

The plan, validated by `poc_explore_dataset_2026-04-30.R`. Single
source of truth; no other section in this document holds phasing.

### 7.1 Pre-decisions (resolved before Phase 1 starts)

Three open questions from the design phase, resolved here so Phase 1
proceeds without further debate.

**(a) DE column names: AnnData-canonical wins.**
The API exposes `effect_log2fc` / `score_pvalue` / `score_fdr`
(matching the AnnData spec's `varm["de_<c>"]` columns). Reason: those
are the names the H5AD subclass will naturally produce; using them in
the SE subclasses too means the column-rename boundary stays
identical across backends. Modules currently reading `log2Ratio` /
`pValue` / `fdr` rename at their `dplyr::select()` boundary — see
§6.4.

**(b) Per-group means: legacy shim materialises them in Phase 1;
computed accessor lands in Phase 2.**
Today's modules read `seqAnno$<assay>_<group>_Mean` /
`<assay>_<group>_SD` columns built by `convert_genomics_se()`.
Phase 1's `legacy_gStoreList_from_eds()` reproduces these exactly so
the shim is truly drop-in. When a Phase 2 module migration needs
them, it switches from the column read to a new accessor
`eds$assay_group_means(contrast, assay)` (added to the contract by
the first migration PR that needs it).

**(c) Producer-side migration is a separate workstream.**
Tracked in
[`producer_migration_2026-04-30.md`](producer_migration_2026-04-30.md).
exploreDE is unaffected by its timeline — until producers migrate,
the SE subclasses do their job; afterwards, the H5AD subclass
handles every input and the SE subclasses retire.

### 7.3 Phase 1 — Wire into the running app via legacy shim

The bottleneck phase. Builds `legacy_gStoreList_from_eds()` and
modifies the existing `convert_*_se()` / `inputDataReactive()` so the
running app uses the new infrastructure under the hood, while every
server module continues to read from the legacy `gStoreList$X` shape.

**Files to add / modify:**

- `R/legacy_glue.R` — `legacy_gStoreList_from_eds(eds, se = NULL)`
  produces all 23 gStoreList fields the audit enumerated:
  `allPathways`, `contrasts`, `countList`, `dataset`, `dataType`,
  `design`, `designLevels`, `factorLevels`, `factorNames`, `factors`,
  `gene_choices`, `gene_lookup`, `genes`, `goObjects`, `groupingName`,
  `param`, `protein_choices`, `protein_lookup`, `se`, `seqAnno`,
  `seqAnnoList`, `seUnfiltered`, `sgRNA_to_gene`. Each field is
  derived from `eds$method()` calls + a few computations (per-group
  means, log2 transforms, `seqAnno`-shape construction). ~250 lines.
- `R/helperFunctions.R` — `convert_genomics_se()` body becomes:
  ```r
  eds <- new_explore_dataset(se)
  legacy_gStoreList_from_eds(eds, se = se)   # se passed for $se field
  ```
  Same for `convert_proteomics_se()`.
- `inst/app/server-initInputData.R` — `inputDataReactive()` returns
  `c(gStoreList, list(.eds = eds))` so old `inputDataReactive()$X`
  reads still work AND new `inputDataReactive()$.eds` is available.

**Tests:**

- `test-legacy-shim-equivalence.R` — for each demo dataset, run the
  OLD `convert_genomics_se()` (snapshot from before Phase 1) and the
  NEW shim'd version, assert field-by-field equivalence on every
  gStoreList field.

**Acceptance:** equivalence tests pass; in-app smoke test on each of
the 6 demo datasets — no visual regressions.

The H5AD peer subclass lands here. Until producers migrate, this is

### 7.6 Phase 4a — Bring-your-own-data (BYOD)

The "FGCZ-agnostic" goal from the Overview lands here. Architectural
support for BYOD exists from Phase 3 (the factory accepts any input
that yields a canonical `AnnData`); Phase 4a is the documentation +
UX work that makes BYOD actually usable by external researchers.

**Deliverables:**

- `vignettes/byod.Rmd` — "minimum viable AnnData" guide, worked
  examples per omics modality (RNA-seq counts, proteomics
  intensities, CRISPR sgRNA counts), step-by-step CSV → `.h5ad`
  walkthrough.
- `R/csv_to_canonical_anndata.R` — helper for the common BYOD case
  of `counts.csv` + `samples.csv` + `features.csv` + optional
  `de_<contrast>.csv`. Produces a conformant `.h5ad` with the right
  factor encoding, `var_names` setup, `uns` metadata.
- Friendly validator error messages with field-by-field diagnosis
  (the schema validator from §4.2 wrapped in a UI surface that
  guides users to fix their `.h5ad`).
- App entry point that accepts a local `.h5ad` upload (not just
  gStore/pStore URLs) — the running app today routes everything
  through SUSHI/B-Fabric path conventions; Phase 4a generalises this
  so a researcher can drag a file in.

**Acceptance:** a researcher with no FGCZ access loads exploreDE,
points it at their own canonical `.h5ad`, and gets the same app
experience as an internal user with a SUSHI dataset.

## 8. Open questions

Two questions remain unresolved. Both are Phase-2-time decisions —
**they MUST be answered before the relevant Phase 2 PR is opened**,
not before. Listed here so they aren't forgotten.

### 8.1 — OPEN — Methods-text panel rendering strategy

**Decide at**: Tier 2.5 — when migrating `server-summary.R`.

**The question.** Today `server-summary.R` renders a `kable()` table
of `metadata(se)$param` (SUSHI parameters that produced the analysis:
`comparison`, `sampleGroup`, `featureLevel`, `refBuild`, `runGO`,
FDR thresholds, etc.) The canonical AnnData has no `param` — those
fields decompose across `uns$de`, `uns$design`, `uns$omics_type`,
`uns$reference_genome`, `uns$app_hints`, `uns$provenance`. Two
strategies:

- **Pre-render** the prose to HTML/markdown at converter time, stash
  on `uns$provenance$methods_text`, expose via `eds$methods_text()`.
  Module just prints the string. (Frozen at converter time but
  simple.)
- **Reconstruct** the table from canonical slots at render time
  using `eds$contrast_meta(c)`, `eds$ref_build()`, etc.
  (Module owns the formatting; flexible.)

**Status**: undecided.

**My lean** (not a decision): reconstruct at render time, so modules
own their UI formatting and the API just exposes data. But the call
belongs to whoever migrates `server-summary.R`.

---

### Resolved (kept here for the audit trail)

- ~~Method vs. free-function call style.~~ → **pure R6** method-call
  style (`eds$samples()`, `eds$de(c)`). No free-function wrapper
  layer. Resolved 2026-04-30.
- ~~Per-shape SE subclasses vs single canonical-AnnData reader at
  load time.~~ → **per-shape SE subclasses + future H5AD peer
  subclass.** Multiple small subclasses are easier to read and
  document than a single reader plus a converter with branchy `if
  (shape == ...)` logic. The on-disk canonical `.h5ad` direction is
  unchanged. Resolved 2026-04-30 evening (pivoted from an earlier
  same-day canonical-converter choice).
- ~~`contrast_label(c)` helper or not.~~ → **helper ships in the
  base class.** Returns the canonical contrast key verbatim (already
  in `test_vs_reference` identifier-safe form) after validating the
  contrast exists. Modules wanting prose for plot titles use
  `gsub("_vs_", " vs ", contrast_label(c))`. Implemented in
  `ExploreDataset.R` during Phase 2 (server-correlation.R
  migration). Resolved 2026-05-15.

## Appendix A — Alternative design considered

Before settling on the per-shape SE subclass design, a single-reader
design was considered:

- One concrete `ExploreDatasetH5AD` reader from day 1
- A free function `se_to_canonical_anndata()` that normalised every
  legacy SE shape into canonical AnnData at load time, with four
  per-shape implementations (`.se_to_canon_rnaseq`, `_count_qc`,
  `_crispr_count_qc`, `_proteomics`)
- All SE-shape knowledge concentrated in the converter; the reader
  walked canonical slots uniformly

The argument for that design was: fewer reader classes, mechanically
enforced spec compliance at load, free `.h5ad` export from any
input.

Rejected in favour of the subclass design because:

- **Readability and documentation.** Four small subclasses with
  shape-specific knowledge co-located are easier to follow than a
  single converter function with branchy `if (shape == ...)` logic.
- **Independent evolution.** Subclasses can absorb shape-specific
  quirks (e.g. proteomics' built `feature_id` and `fid_lookup`)
  without leaking into a shared canonicalisation step.
- **Same downstream contract.** Both designs expose the same
  accessor API to modules; the choice is invisible above the
  intermediate layer.

The on-disk canonical `.h5ad` direction is unchanged either way. The
SE → AnnData mapping logic that would have lived in
`se_to_canonical_anndata()` is preserved in `build_example_anndata.R`
as the reference for upstream producers and as the source-of-truth
for the eventual `$as_anndata()` export methods (if we add them per
the §1.7 note).
